svg.title: Ideological layers and institutions of Greater Germany
svg.desc: Five ideological layers in the Greater German Reich connected to the principal institutions that reproduced or administered them.
svg.text: Ideology and institutions in Greater Germany
A long-lived order reproduces belief through different audiences, offices, and material systems

g.text: IDEOLOGICAL LAYER
PRINCIPAL INSTITUTIONAL CARRIERS
1 · Public civil religion
Volk, founder memory, victory, family, work, service, memorial
Propaganda Ministry · schools · youth · ceremonies
Broad language compatible with Christian or private ambiguity
2 · Party orthodoxy
Racial history, obedience, class subordination, empire, doctrine
Party Chancellery · Gau network · institutes · courts
Canonical texts and authentic interpretation after Hitler
3 · SS racial order
Ancestry, marriage, oath, settlement, security, graded inclusion
RuSHA · Lebensborn · Ahnenerbe · police · Waffen-SS
Order Faith adds theology but does not define the whole Reich
4 · Technical-administrative doctrine
Databases, health indices, settlement, labor, schools, transport
Ministries · doctors · engineers · statisticians · firms
Ideological objectives presented as objective administration
5 · Private belief and quiet nonbelief
Believers, Christians, beneficiaries, conformists, cynics, dissenters
Households · churches · workplaces · settler communities
Compliance does not prove conviction; enforcement still operates
Institutions overlap and compete. The SS can dominate eastern status law without controlling every railway, factory, church, or ministry.
